title: Operations Key Account Manager
description:
Overview
Microsoft partners are central to how Microsoft reaches and serves customers. The Partner Enablement organization, within Microsoft Business Operations, helps partners understand, prepare for, implement, and adopt changes across the partner lifecycle.
The role independently leads complex, cross-functional partner enablement programs that bridge Microsoft strategy and partner execution. The Operations Key Account Manager develops a deep understanding of partner business models, capabilities, dependencies, and operational experiences; translates partner insight into clear recommendations and actionable business requirements; identifies and communicates risks early; and drives readiness and adoption for priority launches and change moments. Acting as a trusted advisor and Voice of Partner, this role is expected to create clarity in ambiguous situations, influence decisions without direct authority, and deliver measurable outcomes that reduce friction, strengthen trust, and improve the ease of doing business with Microsoft.
Scope
Operates independently on complex programs with broad cross-functional dependencies and material partner or business impact.
Moves from analysis to a clear point of view, recommendation, and action plan; uses sound judgment to make progress when direction is incomplete.
Leads through influence rather than formal authority, aligning stakeholders on outcomes, ownership, decisions, and timelines.
Anticipates risks and dependencies, escalates with context and options, and drives issues to resolution with appropriate urgency.
Communicates concise, decision-ready updates for leadership and adapts detail for partner, technical, operational, and executive audiences.
Creates reusable approaches, operating rhythms, standards, and scalable solutions that improve outcomes beyond a single launch or partner.
Leads the partner-facing change-management workstream from early impact assessment through sustained adoption, while keeping ownership of product, policy, platform, and technical delivery with the originating teams.
Facilitates structured co-design among partners, engineering, product, business planning, operations, and launch teams to test assumptions, shape requirements, validate implementation feasibility, and resolve readiness risks before launch commitments are finalized.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond
Responsibilities
Partner Lifecycle Enablement and Trusted Advisory
Drive partner enablement across end-to-end partner lifecycle processes to reduce friction and improve the ease of doing business with Microsoft.
Build trusted relationships and structured engagement rhythms that surface partner priorities, operational pain points, requirements, risks, and emerging needs.
Develop a practical understanding of partner business models, capabilities, technical and operational dependencies, and change impacts.
Translate complex Microsoft business, product, engineering, policy, security, compliance, and platform changes into clear partner actions and operational implications.
Voice of Partner and Advocacy
Represent the Voice of Partner across Microsoft, using partner evidence and subject-matter expertise to influence requirements, design, prioritization, roadmaps, and launch decisions.
Assess, clarify, and prioritize partner requirements, converting partner asks into actionable business requirements, recommendations, or experience improvements.
Clearly articulate partner risks and concerns, including tangible business and operational impact, required ownership, and mitigation or risk-acceptance decisions.
Connect individual partner experiences to broader patterns and systemic opportunities, and close the feedback loop with partners and internal stakeholders.
Partner Co-Design and Engineering Collaboration
Plan and facilitate co-design engagements with representative partners and engineering teams for changes that meet defined impact, complexity, or risk criteria.
Frame clear co-design objectives, partner scenarios, decision questions, constraints, and expected outputs so sessions produce actionable evidence rather than general feedback.
Translate partner workflows, technical dependencies, implementation effort, and operational constraints into prioritized requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, or design recommendations for engineering and business owners.
Partner with engineering and product owners to identify what can be influenced, what is fixed, and what requires an explicit trade-off, exception, or risk-acceptance decision.
Coordinate previews, pilots, sandbox or test-environment validation, and implementation walkthroughs to confirm that guidance, tooling, APIs, support paths, and operational processes are usable before broad release.
Document decisions, owners, unresolved issues, and feedback disposition; close the loop with participating partners by explaining what changed, what did not, and why.
Readiness, Adoption, and Change Management
Own the partner change-management and readiness plan for priority launches and key change moments, including the change narrative, impacted partner segments, required partner actions, deliverables, milestones, dependencies, measures of success, risks, communications inputs, and stakeholder updates.
Assess change impact and cumulative change burden across partner business models, geographies, roles, technical architectures, operational processes, and overlapping implementation timelines; identify where sequencing, scope, or support must change.
Define readiness criteria and evidence for each change, distinguishing confirmed preparedness, at-risk status, not-ready status, and unknown status; use these signals to inform launch, mitigation, escalation, and exception decisions.
Escalate blockers early with clear business impact, accountable ownership, and resolution needs; drive mitigation before critical milestones and go-live.
Track implementation and adoption through and after go-live, confirm whether required partner actions and intended outcomes were achieved, and transition unresolved issues or sustained support needs to accountable owners.
Data, Scale, and Continuous Improvement
Use preparedness, adoption, operational, business, and qualitative data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and systemic gaps.
Define measurable success criteria and deliver concise, decision-ready executive narratives that include a clear assessment, recommendation, trade-offs, and actions required.
Apply a continuous-improvement mindset to standardize services, simplify processes, reduce manual work, and advance automation, AI-enabled insights, and self-service enablement models.
Balance high-touch partner engagement with scalable and preventative solutions that address recurring friction across the broader ecosystem.
Cross-Functional Leadership
Demonstrate a One Microsoft approach by working seamlessly across engineering, business planning, product and launch, sales, operations, support, compliance, and enablement teams.
Create clarity on accountability, decisions, and next steps; independently convene and align the right stakeholders to solve ambiguous, cross-organizational problems.
Influence without direct authority using partner evidence, sound judgment, business impact, and data; confidently recommend a path forward when information is incomplete.
Demonstrate thought leadership, strategic thinking, adaptability, and proactive identification of end-to-end opportunities that drive business impact.
Success in This Role
Partners understand the change, know what actions are required, and are prepared to implement and adopt it with greater confidence and less friction.
Partner requirements and risks are surfaced early enough to influence design, launch, process, policy, or operational decisions.
Readiness plans provide an honest, timely view of progress, dependencies, blockers, ownership, and decisions required.
Partner insights are translated into measurable improvements and scalable solutions rather than repeated one-off interventions.
Cross-functional teams have clear accountability and shared understanding of partner impact, priorities, and outcomes.
Representative partners and engineers have validated critical scenarios, requirements, technical guidance, and implementation paths early enough to influence the solution or make explicit risk decisions.
Readiness status is evidence-based, distinguishes known risk from unknown status, and drives timely decisions on sequencing, mitigation, exceptions, and launch confidence.
Change-management plans address partner awareness, understanding, capability, implementation, adoption, reinforcement, and closed-loop learning rather than stopping at communications or launch completion.
Embody our  culture  and  values
Qualifications
Minimum / Required Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 4+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR equivalent experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience, OR equivalent experience.
Experience working in global, cross-functional, and highly matrixed environments.
Proven record of delivering complex programs, launches, operational changes, or improvement initiatives with competing priorities.
Demonstrated experience in partner channel management, partner operations, customer relationship management, customer success, or strategic account engagement.
Ability to translate technical, operational, and business requirements into clear plans, recommendations, and executive-ready communications.
Strong project and change-management capability, including change-impact assessment, stakeholder and resistance planning, readiness criteria, adoption measurement, navigating ambiguity, resolving conflict, negotiating trade-offs, and developing practical solutions.
Strong analytical capability using data, reporting, dashboards, KPIs, and qualitative insight to influence decisions and monitor outcomes.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex subjects to global audiences and engage effectively across levels and cultures.
Demonstrated impact and influence skills, including cross-boundary collaboration and relationship building with internal and external stakeholders.
Experience identifying systemic issues and applying industry practices, standardization, automation, AI, continuous improvement, or self-service solutions to improve scale and sustainability.
Understanding of cloud, commerce, digital platforms, partner ecosystems, security, compliance, or lifecycle operations is advantageous.
Independent, flexible, proactive, and able to identify strategic opportunities, develop proposals, and gain stakeholder alignment.
Core Capabilities
Partner Advocacy and Voice of Partner | Partner Co-Design and Engineering Collaboration | Strategic Business Analysis | Program and Change Management | Readiness and Adoption | Data-Informed Decision Making | Risk Management | Executive Communication | Cross-Functional Influence | Relationship Management | Continuous Improvement | Automation and Scale

Critical Environment Culture Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
May travel up to 25%, typically domestically for training and/or supporting another site. May work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting up to 25lbs / 11kg without assistance. Occasional lifting 25-50lbs / 11-22.5kg with lift assistance. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria
Equipment and Systems Maintenance Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities. Advises engineer partners or project management colleagues on project scope process or execution methodology. Presents for review and approval MSOW in their area of responsibility.
Acts as a subject matter expert, performing troubleshooting independently for multiple equipment, systems, subsystems, and component types. Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment in all disciplines work and how to troubleshoot to subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. Oversees less experienced colleagues, or directly troubleshooting systems and investigates root causes.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs for multiple disciplines and multiple equipment types of increasing complexity with no supervision, while serving as a subject matter expert for one discipline - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Provides consultation to colleagues on maintenance and repairs through deep understanding of equipment, systems and their interrelations. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees everyday, complex, large-scale tasks for a single discipline or equipment across disciplines. Ensures follow up action items are addressed in a timely manner. Masters the maintenance of all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance across all disciplines. Plans, coordinates, and presents maintenance items for review and approval in their area of responsibility.
Prepares and submits highly complex reports as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Root Cause Analysis [RCA] reports) and may review prior reports delivered by less experienced team members. Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for highly complex and/or interdependent equipment and disciplines to ensure safe and reliable execution. Reviews completed work using approved tools and procedural templates from less experienced technicians for accuracy and completeness. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on all procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates across all LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Coordinates with vendor to schedule maintenance and determines availability of equipment/parts, as directed. Resolves or escalates observed vendor quality issues. May review and approve vendor supplier field service reports, invoices, and work orders.
Equipment and Systems Operations Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides and/or leads and coordinates emergency monitoring response plans for irregular or malfunctioning conditions. Serves as technical expert in ensuring emergency operating procedures (EOPs) are consistent with proper incident response.
Serves as an expert in the inspection and supervision of critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions. Understands critical system alarms for multiple discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) and understands risks or impacts to other subsystems across the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements. Uses data trends to develop or produce predictive analyses of equipment performance.
Works on complex, advanced tasks (e.g., stabilization, resolution, recovery) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, advises less experienced colleagues on such topics, and provides oversight and training/mentorship to team members on tasks regarding these subsystems (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls, generators). Demonstrates an understanding of and operates equipment and systems across all disciplines (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Tracks utilization and time tracking results for team members, within applicable task management systems, as needed. Guides and coaches team in CMMS usage best practices. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications: High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.
5+ years mission critical services work/applied learning experience (e.g., high availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or related fields) OR equivalent experience.
1+ year(s) experience in a specialized area (e.g., mechanical field, electrical field, controls field) or related field.
Other Requirements:  Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:  Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

OpenAI's Compute organization builds and operates the infrastructure that powers frontier AI training and inference. Our data center engineering teams develop the technical standards and infrastructure required to deploy compute at unprecedented scale across both self-built and partner-operated environments.

We work across civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, construction, and infrastructure delivery to develop data center designs that are reliable, scalable, and optimized for speed.

We are seeking a Data Center Design Manager to coordinate the design and delivery of infrastructure for large-scale AI deployments.

You will bring engineering disciplines and external design partners together to translate infrastructure requirements into coordinated, buildable design packages. You will manage design milestones, resolve cross-discipline interfaces, and keep technical decisions aligned with project requirements.

description:
About the Role

As a Financial Systems Engineer, you will design, build, and operate the financial systems and integrations that support critical accounting processes across Oracle Fusion Cloud and OpenAI’s broader finance technology ecosystem. You’ll partner with Corporate Accounting, Accounts Payable, Revenue Accounting, Supply Chain, Engineering, Data, Tax, and other cross-functional teams to deliver reliable, scalable, and auditable solutions.

This role requires deep Oracle Financials expertise, strong accounting process knowledge, and an engineering mindset. You will work across corporate accounting processes including equity, payroll, accruals, leases, mergers and acquisitions, intercompany, and close; transform Accounts Payable processes; and design solutions for complex supply chain accounting, cost accounting, ASC 606 revenue recognition, and compute and data-center accounting. You’ll help redefine how finance teams work by applying automation, AI, and agentic approaches to reduce manual effort, strengthen controls, and accelerate accounting and close processes.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the solution design, delivery, and continuous improvement of Oracle Fusion Financials and connected finance platforms, acting as both a hands-on engineer and a trusted functional partner.

 - Partner with Corporate Accounting to improve processes for equity, payroll, expense accruals, lease accounting, mergers and acquisitions, reconciliations, and the month-end and quarter-end close.

 - Work with Accounts Payable to deliver transformation initiatives across invoice intake, validation, matching, approvals, accounting, payments, supplier experience, exception management, and operational reporting.

 - Strong knowledge of corporate accounting processes, including equity, payroll, expense accruals, lease accounting, mergers and acquisitions, reconciliations, and financial close.

 - Hands-on experience transforming Accounts Payable processes and integrating procurement, invoicing, tax, payments, suppliers, and reporting capabilities.

 - Deep understanding of supply chain accounting, Supply Chain Financial Orchestration, inventory and cost accounting, standard and landed costs, purchase price variance, logistics costs, and cost of goods sold.

 - Strong knowledge of ASC 606 and experience designing Oracle-integrated accounting solutions for hardware, supply chain, and other complex or nonstandard revenue arrangements in partnership with Revenue Accounting and Engineering teams.

Employee Technology & Experience helps people at OpenAI do their most ambitious work. Across Helpdesk, Executive Support, Systems Operations, Logistics and audiovisual services, we make technology simple, reliable and secure. Employee needs guide what we build, improve and eliminate.

IT Logistics keeps employees equipped, from day 1 readiness to timely replacements and self-service peripherals. We manage the full equipment lifecycle and improve access to hardware as employee needs evolve.

We’re hiring an IT Logistics Lead to manage the team that keeps OpenAI employees equipped for their most important work. You’ll run daily operations, evaluate new hardware and introduce equipment and services that address unmet needs.

You’ll own the hardware and peripheral catalog, fulfillment programs, asset management systems and regional operating models. You’ll deliver on IT’s promise: equipment ready on day 1 globally, choices suited to each employee’s location and work, self-service employees trust, and accurate records of what we own, where it is and who has it.

This is a hands-on people management role. You’ll coach team members, manage performance and work alongside them on execution and escalations. With your manager, you’ll set priorities and plan capacity. As customer zero, you’ll use OpenAI products to solve unresolved logistics problems, continually improving accuracy and shortening lead times.

OpenAI’s Recruiting Operations (RecOps) team provides the systems, workflows, and data foundation that power hiring at OpenAI. We are seeking a Systems & Enablement Lead, Recruiting Operations to lead improvements across recruiting processes, systems, and enablement. You’ll identify recurring friction, define the underlying problem, and carry solutions from an initial test through implementation, adoption, and a repeatable operating process.

You’ll partner with Recruiting leaders, People Systems, and hiring teams to translate hiring priorities into scalable processes and programs. You’ll align stakeholders on the most consequential problems, establish shared operating standards, and lead changes that improve recruiting effectiveness. Success means measurable improvements, sustained adoption, and clear ownership that enables teams to operate independently and adapt as hiring needs evolve.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead projects from discovery through adoption, managing scope, milestones, dependencies, and risks.

 - Owning enablement for operational workflow changes, including documentation, training, office hours, and change communication.

 - Supporting offer approval and other sensitive recruiting workflows through clear coordination, followthrough, and exception handling.

 - Identifying recurring support themes and driving fixes through process changes, documentation improvements, automation, or handoff to People Systems.

title: Manager, Return To Vendor (RTV)
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE IDEAL CANDIDATE:
The Manager, Return to Vendor (RTV) is a key individual contributor within the Sourcing organization responsible for overseeing the end-to-end RTV process across the company's retail and e-commerce supply chain. This role serves as the primary point of contact for vendor return negotiations, disputes, and recovery, ensuring that defective, excess, and non-conforming merchandise is resolved efficiently and that the company maximizes recovery value. The ideal candidate is highly analytical, a skilled negotiator, and comfortable operating cross-functionally with Merchandising, Quality, Logistics, Finance, and Vendor partners.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
RTV Program Ownership
Own and manage the full RTV lifecycle — from claim initiation through resolution, credit receipt, or physical return logistics.
Establish and maintain a centralized RTV tracking system; monitor open claims, aging balances, and recovery rates.
Develop and enforce RTV policies, standard operating procedures, and escalation protocols.
Partner with Buying and Planning teams to identify and prioritize RTV candidates across categories.
Vendor Negotiation & Relationship Management
Lead direct negotiations with vendor partners to secure credits, replacements, or return authorizations in alignment with contractual terms.
Build and maintain productive vendor relationships while assertively advocating for the company's financial interests.
Review and interpret vendor contracts and purchase order terms related to returns, defects, and chargebacks.
Identify recurring quality or compliance issues with vendors and escalate to the Sourcing Director for strategic action.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Collaborate with the Logistics and Warehouse teams to coordinate physical return shipments, disposition of goods, and inbound/outbound documentation.
Partner with Finance and Accounts Payable to ensure timely posting of vendor credits and accurate reconciliation of RTV balances.
Work with the Quality Assurance team to document and report on product defect trends to inform future sourcing decisions.
Support Buying teams during vendor onboarding to ensure RTV terms and expectations are clearly defined.
Reporting & Continuous Improvement
Produce regular reporting on RTV volume, recovery rate, aging claims, and open liabilities for senior leadership review.
Identify process gaps and implement improvements to reduce cycle time, increase recovery, and minimize dispute resolution time.
Benchmark RTV performance against industry standards and recommend best practices.
REQUIREMENTS:
5+ years of experience in sourcing, procurement, vendor management, or supply chain — with direct RTV, chargeback, or vendor compliance exposure.
Demonstrated experience negotiating with vendor partners, including knowledge of contract terms, credit processes, and dispute resolution.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to manage large volumes of data and derive actionable insights.
Proficiency in Google Sheets; experience with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, or equivalent) and inventory/order management platforms.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence without authority across internal teams and external partners.
Highly organized with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple open claims and priorities simultaneously.
All posted ranges are reflective of base salary and may vary depending upon experience level and location. Bonus and equity may also be provided for eligible roles.

Inspect exterior, interior, and vehicle functionality from a customer and trained-observer perspective. Perform static inspections and dynamic road tests, including evaluation of fit and finish, gaps and flush, closures, trim, paint, molding, interfaces, comfort, ergonomics functionality, wind noise, road noise, and other customer-facing attributes. Identify defects objectively and compare conditions against current boundary criteria, Craftsmanship Quality Sheets, gap plans, design intent, benchmarking references, and other approved standards. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary This position is designed for emerging to mid-level Technicians who are eager to grow their technical acumen while delivering an exceptional customer experience. As part of our junior talent pipeline, you will work closely under the mentorship of senior technicians and leadership to support EV repairs, inspections, and field service operations. The ideal candidate thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments, possesses strong communication skills, and brings a passion for innovation and adventure. While based primarily at a local service center, this role may involve remote work, traveling for mobile service, or supporting plant operations as business needs evolve. Responsibilities Vehicle Service & Repair: Perform or assist with assigned vehicle diagnosis, repairs, installations, and inspections—whether at a service center, mobile route, or remote location. Technical Guidance & Learning: Learn to identify and explain the product line, EV framework, tools, and accessories while establishing peer relationships and working under the mentorship of senior technicians. Procedure & Safety Adherence: Utilize available technical resources and follow repair procedures efficiently without compromising quality or safety. Quality Assurance: Conduct road tests on vehicles post-repair to verify repair quality and ensure operational safety. Parts & Operations Management: Assist with day-to-day parts operations, including ordering, receiving, shipping, inventory tracking, and work order/expense reporting. Documentation: Maintain proper, detailed technical notes and documentation for all completed and in-process repairs for internal and external use. Customer Interaction: Perform duties with high professionalism when interacting with customers, families, third-party affiliates, and suppliers at service facilities or outreach events. Continuous Improvement: Identify process areas for improvement, provide constructive feedback to mentorship leads, and participate in service campaigns or containment initiatives. Professional Growth: Actively engage in required training, stay current on evolving technical skills, and maintain high-quality work with minimal supervision as experience increases. Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer is preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including potential shifts on weekends, holidays, early mornings, evenings, or overnights based on business needs. Flexibility for travel to regional locations or production facilities as needed. Proficient with laptops/computers in Windows or Mac environments, as well as work order management systems. Eagerness to learn, strong organizational skills, time management, and high attention to detail. Ability to perform physical tasks, including sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, reaching, and lifting up to 50 lbs. Education & Experience: Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school/program is highly preferred. 0–3 years of hands-on experience in an automotive shop or technical environment; open to recent graduates looking to launch their career. Basic exposure to electric vehicle (EV) / hybrid frameworks, or experience working in fast-paced start-up environments is a plus. Technical Foundations (Junior Level Focus) Electrical & Systems: Foundational understanding of basic electricity theory (high voltage vs. low voltage awareness), basic circuit measurement tools (DVOM), and introductory exposure to reading electrical schematics. Chassis & Maintenance: Familiarity with basic hand and power tools, entry-level tire repairs, and basic vehicle alignments. Diagnostics & Workflows: Basic understanding of diagnostic workflows and troubleshooting steps under guidance. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary This position is designed for emerging to mid-level Technicians who are eager to grow their technical acumen while delivering an exceptional customer experience. As part of our junior talent pipeline, you will work closely under the mentorship of senior technicians and leadership to support EV repairs, inspections, and field service operations. The ideal candidate thrives in dynamic, fast-paced environments, possesses strong communication skills, and brings a passion for innovation and adventure. While based primarily at a local service center, this role may involve remote work, traveling for mobile service, or supporting plant operations as business needs evolve. Responsibilities Vehicle Service & Repair: Perform or assist with assigned vehicle diagnosis, repairs, installations, and inspections—whether at a service center, mobile route, or remote location. Technical Guidance & Learning: Learn to identify and explain the product line, EV framework, tools, and accessories while establishing peer relationships and working under the mentorship of senior technicians. Procedure & Safety Adherence: Utilize available technical resources and follow repair procedures efficiently without compromising quality or safety. Quality Assurance: Conduct road tests on vehicles post-repair to verify repair quality and ensure operational safety. Parts & Operations Management: Assist with day-to-day parts operations, including ordering, receiving, shipping, inventory tracking, and work order/expense reporting. Documentation: Maintain proper, detailed technical notes and documentation for all completed and in-process repairs for internal and external use. Customer Interaction: Perform duties with high professionalism when interacting with customers, families, third-party affiliates, and suppliers at service facilities or outreach events. Continuous Improvement: Identify process areas for improvement, provide constructive feedback to mentorship leads, and participate in service campaigns or containment initiatives. Professional Growth: Actively engage in required training, stay current on evolving technical skills, and maintain high-quality work with minimal supervision as experience increases. Qualifications General & Operational Requirements: High School Diploma, GED, or recognized equivalency credential preferred. Minimum age of 21 years old. Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no suspensions or revocations within the past 3–5 years). Ability to drive a non-commercial truck and trailer is preferred. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including potential shifts on weekends, holidays, early mornings, evenings, or overnights based on business needs. Flexibility for travel to regional locations or production facilities as needed. Proficient with laptops/computers in Windows or Mac environments, as well as work order management systems. Eagerness to learn, strong organizational skills, time management, and high attention to detail. Ability to perform physical tasks, including sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, reaching, and lifting up to 50 lbs. Education & Experience: Graduation from an accredited automotive repair school/program is highly preferred. 0–3 years of hands-on experience in an automotive shop or technical environment; open to recent graduates looking to launch their career. Basic exposure to electric vehicle (EV) / hybrid frameworks, or experience working in fast-paced start-up environments is a plus. Technical Foundations (Junior Level Focus) Electrical & Systems: Foundational understanding of basic electricity theory (high voltage vs. low voltage awareness), basic circuit measurement tools (DVOM), and introductory exposure to reading electrical schematics. Chassis & Maintenance: Familiarity with basic hand and power tools, entry-level tire repairs, and basic vehicle alignments. Diagnostics & Workflows: Basic understanding of diagnostic workflows and troubleshooting steps under guidance. Role Summary This position is designed for emerging to mid-level Technicians who are eager to grow their technical acumen while delivering an exceptional customer experience. Documentation: Maintain proper, detailed technical notes and documentation for all completed and in-process repairs for internal and external use. Customer Interaction: Perform duties with high professionalism when interacting with customers, families, third-party affiliates, and suppliers at service facilities or outreach events. Availability for a standard 40-hour workweek, including potential shifts on weekends, holidays, early mornings, evenings, or overnights based on business needs. Flexibility for travel to regional locations or production facilities as needed. Proficient with laptops/computers in Windows or Mac environments, as well as work order management systems. Eagerness to learn, strong organizational skills, time management, and high attention to detail. Ability to perform physical tasks, including sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, reaching, and lifting up to 50 lbs. title: Staff or Senior Firmware Engineer
description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.
Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About this role:
Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.
As a Senior Embedded Software Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.
We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.
Click here to learn more about Samsara's cultural philosophy.
In this role, you will:
Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and argue for the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
Own the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.
Raise the bar for the engineers around you. At the Senior level, you are a force multiplier for your team. Through thoughtful designs, rigorous reviews, hands-on mentorship, and sound technical judgment, you help other engineers deliver better work. You lead by example, strengthen engineering practices, and connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes. You bring clarity to ambiguous problems, act with intellectual honesty and urgency, and deliver high-quality solutions iteratively.
What you bring
8+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , You have delivered reliable firmware where memory, processing power, energy and timing are all scarce, and you know how to measure, optimize and make deliberate trade-offs between them.
You have led firmware development for several new products end to end. You have taken firmware from initial concept through architecture, technical implementation, validation, and product launch, providing hands-on technical leadership throughout.
Substantial bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
You have brought up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
Senior-level scope. You have led work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have consistently driven consensus across teams.
Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you make that trade-off on purpose.
Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
You ship fast without shipping badly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.

title: CV/ML Camera Test Engineer
description:
Company Background
Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.


﻿﻿The Role﻿
Specter is hiring a hands-on CV/ML camera test engineer to measure how camera and optics choices affect the performance of our AI models. Working with our Optics & Camera Engineering Lead, this individual will turn experiment plans into lab and field setups, run the campaigns, push the data through our CV/ML models and report what changed and why. The work is scientific at its core: reason from first principles about optics, sensor physics and illumination, form a hypothesis, design a controlled experiment to test it, and let the data decide. This individual will collaborate with camera, CV/ML, software, hardware and field teams to put data behind every camera decision.

Responsibilities:

 - Form testable hypotheses from first principles (optics, sensor physics, radiometry and illumination), and design controlled experiments with defined variables, controls, sample sizes and success criteria before collecting data.

 - Execute experiments comparing sensors, lenses, ISP settings, IR illumination, focus and window conditions, and measure their effect on detection, recognition and LPR performance at range.

 - Build and maintain lab and outdoor test setups, including targets at known distances, controlled lighting and low-light scenes, IR illumination and chamber runs across temperature.

 - Run field data-collection campaigns across sites, times of day, lighting and weather, keeping conditions, metadata and ground truth consistent.

 - Run captured video through existing CV/ML models and evaluation tools, and compute model metrics alongside image-quality measurements (MTF, SNR, distortion, pixels on target).

 - Script captures, camera settings, data pipelines and analysis in Python and shell on embedded Linux devices so every run is reproducible.

 - Isolate the cause of performance changes across optics, sensor, ISP, illumination and environment, using statistical analysis rather than anecdote, and write clear reports that state confidence, limitations and recommendations.

 - Support camera validation (focus stability, thermal, condensation, IR range) through EVT, DVT and PVT.



Qualifications:

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment and being scrappy.

 - Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent.

 - 2+ years of experience in hardware test, validation or experimental work.

 - Strong Linux command line proficiency (required), including SSH, logs, file and process management and shell scripting on embedded devices.

 - Proficient in Python for scripting, data processing and analysis.

 - A scientific, first-principles mindset: you reason from the physics to predict results, design controlled experiments to test those predictions, and change your mind when the data says so.

 - Hands-on with test setups and lab equipment, and comfortable doing outdoor field work, including at night and in bad weather.

 - Strong grounding in statistics and experimental design, including hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, variance, sample sizing and trends across campaigns.

 - Exceptional organization and communication skills (both written and oral).

 - No CV/ML background required. You'll use our existing models and evaluation tools and learn the rest on the job.



Nice to Have

 - Experience with cameras, image sensors, lenses or image-quality testing (MTF, SNR, low light, IR).

 - Exposure to computer vision tools (OpenCV) or ML evaluation metrics such as precision and recall.

 - Experience with video tooling such as FFmpeg, GStreamer or V4L2.

 - Experience with thermal chambers, reliability or production test.

 - Background in physics, optics or a research lab environment.


Tool Proficiency

 - Linux command line and shell scripting (required).

 - Python with NumPy, pandas and plotting libraries.

 - Git for scripts and test procedures.

 - Imatest or equivalent image-quality tools (preferred).

title: Optics & Camera Engineering Lead
description:
Company Background
Specter's mission is to help automate the physical world.

Today, we build video sensors with state-of-the-art AI agents that answer any question, anywhere in their environments. Our systems can automatically detect and reason about any physical activity captured on camera, from security incidents (e.g. perimeter intrusion, theft, LPR), to safety monitoring (e.g. PPE detection, injured people), to operational efficiency (e.g. material tracking, congestion monitoring). We offer both long range wireless (1km range) and wired sensor variants to suit any deployment.

Our co-founders Xerxes and Philip are passionate about empowering our partners in the fast approaching world of physical AI and robotics. We are a small, fast growing team who hail from Anduril, Tesla, Uber, and the U.S. Special Forces.


﻿﻿The Role﻿
Specter is hiring an Optics & Camera Engineering Lead to own camera performance across our product portfolio. This individual will own the imaging stack end to end: sensor and lens selection, optical requirements tied to CV/ML and customer outcomes, vendor and JDM programs, test campaigns and results analysis, and high volume production. This individual will collaborate with systems, software, CV/ML, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, supply chain and test teams to deliver performant, scalable and validated camera + optical systems to the field.

The role spans the full stack. One day you'll be benchmarking sensors and lenses for a new product. Next, you'll work with our CV/ML team to translate detection, recognition and LPR performance at range into pixel density, MTF and low-light targets, or review athermal lens designs, define a slant-edge MTF test across temperature, or analyze a wiper endurance run. You'll work with systems, software, electrical, mechanical, manufacturing and supply chain, and lead technical engagements with tier-one optics and sensor suppliers.



Responsibilities:

Select sensors and lenses

 - Evaluate and select image sensors for each product, comparing low-light performance (SNR1s, QE at 850/940 nm), pixel size, resolution, frame rate, HDR, supply life and cost.

 - Select off-the-shelf lenses or specify custom designs matched to each sensor: FOV, F-number, MTF across the field, NIR correction, distortion, relative illumination and athermal behavior.

 - Evaluate and select the ISP architecture (on-sensor, companion ASIC/FPGA or SoC ISP), weighing image quality, latency, power, cost and supply, and drive ISP tuning and pipeline development for day and NIR night modes.

 - Benchmark sensor and lens candidates side by side in the lab and the field, and keep a qualified roster of sensors, lenses and IR-cut filters ready for new programs.

Connect customer value to optical requirements

 - Translate customer use cases and CV/ML performance into camera requirements using pixel-density frameworks such as IEC 62676-4 DORI.

 - Run coverage and range trade studies across sensor resolution, FOV, mounting height, pixel density, IR range, inference load, power and cost.

 - Define MTF, aperture, distortion, relative illumination, stray light and NIR focus targets, and tie them to measured model precision and recall at distance.

 - Design and run real-world field test campaigns across sites, lighting and weather, and use the resulting model and image-quality data to close the loop from camera change to quantified customer impact and drive design decisions.

Own optical and camera system design

 - Own optical performance specifications for fixed, multi-camera, panoramic and PTZ products.

 - Integrate the selected sensor, lens, IR-cut filter and mount into a camera system that meets spec across every operating condition.

 - Drive athermal design so focus and MTF hold across a wide operating range under solar loading, accounting for IR-cut filters, lens mounts, flange CTE, humidity and pressure.

 - Specify NIR illumination (LED and laser) matched to lens FOV, including frame-synced strobing, IEC 60825-1 eye safety, thermal limits and internal-reflection control.

 - Guide window, coating, heater, wiper and sun-shade design so optical performance survives years of outdoor service.

 - Use optical simulation to evaluate concepts quickly and review supplier prescriptions with confidence.

Lead vendor and JDM programs

 - Own the technical content of RFPs for camera modules and complete camera systems, and evaluate proposals on performance, cost, schedule and risk.

 - Lead technical work with optics suppliers and ODM/JDM partners on off-the-shelf selection, custom lens design, active alignment and production test.

 - Hold partners to design reviews and gate criteria from design through EVT, DVT and PVT.

Build test capability and run campaigns

 - Grow Specter's optical lab: collimators, slant-edge MTF, focus through temperature, flare and stray light, low-light SNR, IR range and FOV/distortion measurement.

 - Design and qualify optical test equipment for development, reliability and manufacturing, with documented gauge R&R.

 - Plan and run lab reliability and qualification campaigns covering thermal, humidity, condensation, solar loading, ingress, cleaning and coating endurance, and field life, then analyze results and drive decisions.

 - Define calibration (intrinsics, extrinsics, per-unit data) and production acceptance tests at our contract manufacturers.

Scale to production and grow the team

 - Take camera systems from concept to volume production with partners and CMs, driving design for manufacturability, automated focus and alignment, and yield.

 - Partner with embedded imaging engineers on sensor bring-up, driver integration and day/night switching in production.

 - Mentor engineers across camera, image quality, test and manufacturing engineering.

 - Track emerging imaging technology (large-format sensors, zoom optics, EO/IR fusion, camera arrays, computational imaging) and recommend where Specter should invest.



Qualifications:

 - 8+ years in optical, imaging or camera systems engineering, with multiple camera products shipped to volume production.

 - Fluency across the stack, from how image quality affects CV/ML and the end user down to lens design, mechanics and test.

 - Deep knowledge of image sensors, lens design and the trade-offs among resolution, FOV, F-number, MTF, aberrations, depth of focus and thermal stability.

 - Hands-on optical simulation with Zemax OpticStudio, CODE V or similar.

 - A track record specifying off-the-shelf and custom lenses with suppliers, with clear performance and cost trade-offs.

 - Athermalization experience covering both mechanical design and optical performance across temperature (focus shift, MTF drift).

 - Experience designing optical test equipment and running test campaigns, with rigorous data analysis behind decisions.

 - Experience with NIR imaging and active illumination, as well as L/M/SWIR systems.

 - Experience taking hardware through NPI with contract manufacturers or ODM/JDM partners.

 - Clear communication of optical trade-offs to software, business and customer-facing teams.



Nice to Have

 - Outdoor, automotive or security camera experience, including sealing, condensation, window cleaning and environmental qualification.

 - Active alignment and high-volume camera module manufacturing.

 - PTZ, zoom/focus optics, panoramic or multi-camera systems, and camera calibration for computer vision.

 - EO/IR (thermal) imaging.

 - GMSL/FPD-Link camera interfaces and ISP tuning.

 - Laser illumination and eye-safety certification.

 - Experience leading engineers and cross-functional technical programs.
   

Tool Proficiency

 - Zemax OpticStudio, CODE V or equivalent optical design software.

 - Imatest or equivalent image quality analysis tools.

 - Python or MATLAB for test automation and data analysis.

 - Familiarity with MCAD (SolidWorks) for opto-mechanical review.

 - Computer vision fundamentals and tools (OpenCV or similar) for image analysis, calibration and evaluating model performance.

 - Linux command line for sensor bring-up, data capture and scripting on embedded systems.

 - Hardware reliability and test methods: environmental qualification, accelerated life testing, FMEA and failure analysis.

title: Account Executive - Bridge
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the Team
The Account Management team at Bridge is dedicated to the growth, retention, and expansion of key customers. Our Scaled Account Management team focuses on driving measurable expansion across a broad portfolio of mid-market and high-growth customers through data-driven strategies, efficient processes, and strong cross-functional partnership.
What You'll Do
As a Scaled Account Manager at Bridge you will own a book of existing accounts and be responsible for expanding revenue, identifying product gaps and driving product adoption, preventing churn and ensuring renewals at scale. You will combine consultative selling with volume playbooks, prioritization based on quantitative signals, and hands-on execution to identify and close upsell opportunities across your territory. As Bridge continues to develop within Stripe’s Money Management organization, you will also drive your customers’ adoption of additional features available through Stripe.
Responsibilities
- Own a book of existing accounts and drive revenue growth through additional usage, upsells, cross-sells, and renewals.
- Develop and execute scalable go-to-market strategies that increase revenue per account and accelerate product adoption across your portfolio.
- Use data and quantitative analysis to prioritize accounts and identify the highest-impact expansion opportunities.
- Generate leads through targeted outreach, research, and campaign execution; manage high-velocity deal cycles from qualification to close.
- Build strong relationships with customer stakeholders to understand business priorities, surface pain points, and tailor Bridge solutions.
- Lead commercial negotiations and renewals to expand and retain customer revenue.
- Identify churn signals in your book and implement strategies to prevent revenue losses.
- Coordinate with product, success, risk, and operations teams to solve complex customer needs and ensure a great user experience.
- Translate customer feedback into actionable product and process improvements to better serve scaled customer segments.
Who You Are
-5–8 years of full sales cycle or account management experience focused on existing business accounts; experience managing a large book of accounts or high-velocity portfolio strongly preferred.
- Strong analytical skills with experience using data to prioritize accounts, build business cases, and track outcomes.
- Comfortable understanding technical product requirements and articulating solutions across multiple technology products.
- Demonstrated ability to close upsell opportunities and manage complex pricing or commercial negotiations.
- Excellent operational acumen and proven ability to manage time and prioritize across a high-volume territory.
- Highly motivated, persistent, and effective in ambiguous, fast-paced environments.
- Superior written and verbal communication skills.
- Willingness and ability to work in-office in New York or San Francisco at least three days per week.
Preferred Qualifications
- Previous experience at a high-growth payments, fintech, crypto, or technology company.
- Experience with CRM tools, Excel, and basic SQL or a demonstrated comfort with data tools and analysis.
- Background in working cross-functionally with product, risk, and operations teams to deliver outcomes for customers.
Why Bridge
Join a team that values clear thinking, quantitative rigor, and customer obsession. At Bridge you’ll own meaningful customer outcomes, operate with autonomy, and have the opportunity to shape how we scale revenue across high-potential accounts.

title: Account Executive, Product - Link: Bank Payments & Open Banking
description:

About Stripe

That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Product Sales is a team of deep functional and technical specialists who both lead and advise on deals for the most strategically important products in Stripe’s portfolio.
Stripe is expanding its Link Product Sales team, and this role is focused exclusively on bank payments. As an Account Executive, you will help businesses give their customers a fast, trusted way to pay from a bank account using Stripe’s full stack of payments solutions while accelerating the growth of the Link network. Few roles offer such a direct opportunity to shape and grow one of Stripe’s top company priorities.
What you’ll do
As a founding Account Executive for Bank Payments, you will play a central role in shaping and executing Stripe’s go-to-market strategy for this growing product area. You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, and other GTM teams to build deep product and industry expertise, lead complex deals, and guide in-depth conversations with existing and prospective customers. You will bring customer and market insights back to Stripe, helping influence both the product roadmap and how we take bank payments to market.
Bank payments and account connectivity are also an important part of Link’s broader vision for the future of commerce. Where the opportunity intersects with adjacent Link priorities—such as agentic commerce—you will help explore emerging customer use cases and shape how Stripe brings new experiences to market. This gives you the opportunity to build a focused bank payments business while contributing to some of Stripe’s most forward-looking initiatives.
You are an adept sales professional who can lead business and technical conversations at every level of an organization. You know how to establish value in competitive situations and are energized by products that require deep industry expertise and technical fluency. You are equally comfortable working with customers and internal partners, eager to develop and share expertise, and motivated by the opportunity to build in a fast-moving environment. You are an entrepreneurial self-starter, an exceptional communicator, and an analytical thinker with a record of top performance and making the teams around you better.
Responsibilities
Drive revenue, adoption, and new customer acquisition for Stripe’s bank-payments portfolio across enterprise and platform customers
Create a strategic territory plan, lead outreach efforts, and partner with core account teams to develop a robust, qualified bank payments pipeline
Develop relationships with executive stakeholders and lead business and technical discussions with existing and prospective customers
Advise customers on bank payment use cases and tradeoffs, including conversion, account verification, returns, fraud risk, settlement experience, and costs
Deeply understand Stripe’s bank payments products and competitors, serving as an internal and customer-facing expert on the portfolio and market
Identify early-adopter customers and turn successful engagements into repeatable discovery, positioning, and deal-execution playbooks
Engage with Product and Engineering teams to synthesize customer, win/loss, and competitive feedback that informs Stripe’s product roadmap
Contribute to go-to-market playbooks alongside Product, Marketing, Sales, and Technical Services stakeholders
Work collaboratively across Stripe to shape bank-payment products and solutions that meet customer needs
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Requirements
10+ years of customer facing experience at a leading technology or payments company and a track record of top performance
Experience building trusted advisor relationships with senior business leaders
Proven ability to build strong collaborative working relationships with cross-functional business partners
Self-starter capable of operating independently to drive meaningful business results
Enthusiastic “roll up your sleeves” mentality
Excellent verbal and written communication skills
Ability to understand complex technical requirements and craft solutions across multiple stakeholders
Proven experience to lead complex negotiations involving bespoke commercial agreements
Thrives in a fast-paced environment and changing requirements
True team player - always
Humor is very welcomed
Preferred Qualifications
5+ years of experience selling enterprise payments or technology solutions, ideally in bank payments, open banking, account verification, payment risk, or money movement
Strong understanding of ACH, Pay by Bank, and open banking payment flows, including how conversion, verification, returns, fraud risk, payment guarantees, settlement, and customer experience intersect
Experience launching or scaling a new payments product or category, with a track record of translating early customer wins and market feedback into repeatable go-to-market programs

About Stripe

That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
Self Serve Direct Onboarding helps businesses start using Stripe’s products quickly and confidently. The team builds self-service experiences that guide users through providing business information and completing required checks. We turn complex financial, regulatory, and verification requirements into clear steps, shaping both how quickly businesses can get started and the trust they place in Stripe.
At the heart of this work is a shared product activation experience: a consistent way for businesses to start using new financial capabilities as they grow. This foundation helps users avoid repeating information and makes it simpler for product teams to integrate onboarding into their offerings.
AI creates an opportunity to rethink how businesses get started on Stripe. The team is designing onboarding journeys for users who interact directly through a user interface, work with AI agents, or delegate onboarding to agents entirely. We’re improving today’s experience while building the foundations for agent-led onboarding.
What you’ll do
You’ll set engineering direction in partnership with Product and Design and develop the team delivering it. The role combines improving activation today with shaping how onboarding works for people and AI agents.
You’ll use strong product judgment to decide where to experiment, where to build reusable foundations, and how to measure progress through faster activation, fewer repeated steps, and reliable outcomes. You’ll work across Stripe to align teams and resolve dependencies, while coaching engineers and giving them meaningful ownership.
Responsibilities
Lead engineering planning and execution, partnering closely with Product and Design.
Shape the team’s strategy and roadmap, aligning partners across product engineering, Risk, Compliance, and Operations.
Own delivery from problem definition through rollout and ongoing operation, using experimentation to improve activation while maintaining risk controls.
Uphold high engineering standards across the team’s codebases and development practices.
Turn ambiguous goals into focused plans, resolve dependencies, and balance new capabilities with operational health.
Coach and mentor engineers, provide candid feedback, and support career development tailored to their goals.
Partner with Recruiting to hire engineers and build a diverse, high-performing team.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, we encourage you to apply.
Minimum requirements
4+ years of engineering management experience, directly managing and growing teams of 5+ engineers building and shipping products at scale.
8+ years of full-time software development experience.
Experience building user-facing products, with strong user empathy and product judgment.
Experience turning ambiguous goals into clear priorities and delivering work that depends on multiple teams.
A track record of coaching engineers, supporting their growth, and building an environment of candid feedback, inclusion, and shared ownership.
Technical depth to guide architecture and make pragmatic tradeoffs across user interfaces, APIs, backend workflows, and production reliability.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to align technical and nontechnical partners with different priorities and constraints.
Preferred qualifications
Experience simplifying complex customer journeys and using data, user feedback, and experimentation to evaluate outcomes.
Experience modernizing an established product or architecture while continuing to ship improvements and maintain production reliability.
Experience shipping AI-assisted workflows or agent-facing APIs, with clear approaches to evaluating quality and correctness.

Support Stripe's expansion internationally
Participate in policy matters affecting indirect taxes internationally
